content:
Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to offer users a way to transfer their data and settings from an existing app to a designated replacement app. Here are the details.

iOS to Make App Replacement Easier

While it doesn't happen often, developers occasionally take down an existing app and replace it with a new one, forcing users to move to a separate application.

Although most developers try to make the transition as smooth as possible, when it comes to data that isn't stored in the cloud, the migration process may still require users to handle some of the work themselves.

With iOS 27.2, Apple will address this issue with a system-managed migration flow that can transfer the data and supported settings of an app to its designated replacement app before the old app is deleted.

Based on code available in iOS 27.2 beta 1, users will see the following prompt:

The developer recommends transferring the data and settings from your existing "%1$@" app to the new "%2$@" app. Your iPhone can do this for you now before you start using the new app. When finished, the old app will be deleted from this iPhone.

Users will then be able to choose either "Transfer App Data & Settings" or "Transfer Nothing." If the user declines the migration, iOS will display a second confirmation prompt warning that some preferences (including notification and location settings) may need to be reconfigured.

It's worth noting that this feature appears to be limited to cases where a developer replaces their own app with a designated successor app, rather than migrating data between apps from different developers.

Based on the current implementation, iOS can migrate a range of system-level settings and permissions, including:

  • Privacy, Location, and Health authorization decisions
  • Notification settings, including accessory notification settings
  • Per-app Do Not Disturb and Focus Mode settings
  • App Lock and protection settings
  • CarPlay icon arrangement and compatible widget layouts
  • Live Activities and Live Activities for accessories
  • Access permissions for related accessories
  • LaunchServices preferences, fonts, and capture-related defaults, phone data, and Secure Element services

We'll be keeping a close eye on changes to this framework during the iOS 27.2 beta testing period and report back as we learn more about how developers implement this feature.
